T: C1 to give all of your energy, time, etc.
奉獻，獻出（全部精力、時間等）
C2 If you dedicate a book, play, performance, etc. to someone, you publicly say that it is in that person's honour.
› formal When a building, especially a religious building, is dedicated, there is a ceremony at which it is formally opened for use and its particular purpose is stated.
為（尤指宗教建築）舉行奉獻典禮；為…舉行落成儀式

example: He has dedicated his life to scientific research.
他把自己的一生都奉獻給科學研究工作。
The new president said she would dedicate herself to protecting the rights of the sick and the homeless.
新任總統說她將致力於保護病人和無家可歸者的權利。
The book is dedicated to the author's husband.
作者將此書獻給自己的丈夫。
The church was dedicated on 1 March 1805 to the local Saint Jude.
教堂於1805年3月1日落成以紀念當地的聖裘德。

NONE: C1 believing that something is very important and giving a lot of time and energy to it
盡心盡力的，盡職盡責的
C2 designed to be used for one particular purpose

example: a dedicated father/teacher
盡職盡責的父親／教師
She's completely dedicated to her work.
她對自己的工作十分盡心盡力。
The Green Party is dedicated to protecting the environment.
綠黨致力於環境保護工作。
a dedicated computer
專用電腦
a dedicated sports channel
專門的體育頻道

U: C1 [ U ] the willingness to give a lot of time and energy to something because it is important

C: › [ C ] a statement that says in whose honour something has been written, made, performed, etc.
› [ C ] a ceremony in which a building, especially a religious building, is opened for use and its purpose is stated
（尤指宗教建築的）落成典禮，啟用儀式

example: He has always shown great dedication to the cause.
他對這項事業一直都表現出強烈的奉獻精神。
She thanked the staff for their dedication and enthusiasm.
她感謝全體員工的奉獻精神和工作熱情。
The dedication at the front of the book read "For my Father".
書前面的致謝辭中寫道：「獻給我的父親」。

NONE: › if cells dedifferentiate, they return to an earlier stage of development in order to grow again

example: These tumors are unique because some of them dedifferentiate into benign tumors.
這些腫瘤十分獨特，因為其中一些可以去分化成為良性腫瘤。

NONE: C2 to reach an answer or a decision by thinking carefully about the known facts

example: We cannot deduce very much from these figures.
我們無法從這些數字中推斷出太多東西。
[ + that ] The police have deduced that he must have left his apartment yesterday evening.
警方推斷他肯定是在昨天晚上離開公寓的。

NONE: › to take away an amount or part from a total

example: The player had points deducted (from his score) for arguing with the referee.
那名運動員因與裁判發生爭執而被扣分。

NONE: › A deductible amount can be taken away from a total.
› UK an amount of money that is taken away from an employee's pay before they receive it
（薪資）扣除金額（指在收到薪資時已經被扣除的各項金額）
› US UK excess a part of the cost of an accident, injury, etc. that you agree to pay yourself when you buy insurance
（保險）扣除條款，免賠額（指保險單內規定保險購買人在意外發生時自行承擔的某一數額的損失）

example: Expenses like office phone bills are tax-deductible (= you do not have to pay tax on them).
辦公室電話費等開支可從納稅項中扣除。
Customers can lower insurance premiums by taking higher deductibles.
顧客可以選擇高免賠額來降低保險費。

C or U: C2 [ C or U ] the process of reaching a decision or answer by thinking about the known facts, or the decision that is reached
（根據已知的事實所作出的）推斷，推論；推論所促成的決定
C1 [ C or U ] the calculation of taking an amount or a part of something away from a total or the amount that is taken away
C: › [ C ] US and Australian English UK stoppage an amount that is taken away from the money you are paid before you officially receive it

example: Through a process of deduction, the detectives discovered the identity of the killer.
經過一番仔細推斷，警探們搞清了殺手的身份。
All we can do is make deductions from the available facts.
我們只能根據目前掌握的情況作出各種推論。
The interest I receive on my savings account is paid after the deduction of tax.
付給我的存款利息已經扣了稅。
